data.long_meaning: In Hebrew, Mechiel means 'God of mercy'. This name carries a deep spiritual significance for Christians, reminding us of God's boundless compassion and grace. In the Bible, Mechiel is not found as a given name, but it is mentioned in Psalms 86:5, where it refers to God, the merciful one. The name Mechiel carries the meaning “God of mercy” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew. Parents who choose Mechiel usually hope their child will grow to embody god of mercy and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Mechiel of Brabant, also known as Michael of Brabant, was a medieval saint and the patron saint of Brabant in the Low Countries. He is believed to have lived during the 10th century.
historical_references.context: Mechiel is said to have been a hermit who lived in a cave near Leuven, Belgium. He was known for his piety, miracles, and acts of charity towards the poor. His feast day is celebrated on March 14.

historical_references.reference: Mechiel de Bude, also known as Michel de Montaigu or Michel de Bourgeau, was a French scholar and theologian of the late Middle Ages. He lived during the 14th and early 15th centuries.
historical_references.context: Mechiel de Bude was a professor of theology at the University of Paris and a close advisor to King Charles VI of France. He is best known for his work on the interpretation of Scripture and his advocacy of a more rigorous approach to theological inquiry.
